contentBlocks.body: EF Core performance issues often come from loading too much data, missing indexes, N+1 queries, or tracking entities that only need to be read. A strong answer starts with measurement before changing code.

contentBlocks.body: Look for the generated SQL and the actual query plan when performance matters.

Offset pagination (`Skip(page * size).Take(size)`) gets slower the deeper you page, because the database still reads and discards every skipped row, and it is unstable: a row inserted on page 1 shifts everything and a reader sees a duplicate on page 2. Keyset (seek) pagination remembers the last row the client saw and asks for rows after it. It needs a total order, so add a unique tie-breaker such as `Id` after `DueAt`, and an index that matches, `(UserId, DueAt, Id)`, so each page is a single seek.

    .Where(x => x.UserId == userId && x.DueAt <= now)
    .Where(x => after == null
        || x.DueAt > after.DueAt
        || (x.DueAt == after.DueAt && x.Id.CompareTo(after.Id) > 0))
    .OrderBy(x => x.DueAt).ThenBy(x => x.Id)
    .Take(pageSize + 1) // one extra row tells us whether there is a next page
    .Select(x => new DueReviewDto(x.Id, x.Prompt, x.DueAt))

choices: Use AsNoTracking when you do not update the entities
Load every column just in case
payload.answer: Use AsNoTracking when you do not update the entities
payload.explanation: AsNoTracking avoids change-tracking overhead for read-only projections.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why does OFFSET pagination slow down on deep pages?

choices: The database still reads and discards every skipped row
Indexes stop working after the first page
EF Core disables AsNoTracking for large offsets
Each page opens a new database connection
payload.answer: The database still reads and discards every skipped row
payload.explanation: OFFSET 10000 means producing 10,000 rows only to throw them away. Keyset pagination seeks straight to the first row of the next page.
